app.title: FlowScope
app.summary: A person uploads or picks a flow cytometry file, sets the transform cofactor, subsample size, number of clusters and random seed, and runs a fixed pipeline: compensate, transform, cluster, embed. They look over the result as an embedding coloured by cluster, a bar chart of cluster frequencies, a heatmap of median marker expression per cluster and a per-cluster table. The interface flags clusters that stand out statistically. If a model key is set, the person can also ask an AI model for a suggested gating strategy and for an artifact-or-real call on each flagged cluster. They end with a Markdown report they can download, which records the file's checksum and every setting so the run can be repeated.

task.text: Cluster one cytometry sample's events into populations, flag the clusters that look anomalous, and produce a reproducible report for an analyst to review.

data.text: One instrument file of single-cell events, each measured on many fluorescence and scatter channels, reduced to clusters with per-marker medians and frequencies.
data.item: a cluster of cell events in one sample, with its frequency and median expression of each marker

stage.text: analysing a freshly acquired cytometry sample and screening its clusters for artifacts, before an analyst reviews them

mechanism.text: A sidebar form chooses the file and pipeline settings, and one run button fills a dashboard of linked summaries of the same clustering: an embedding scatter, a frequency bar chart, a marker heatmap and tables. A deterministic anomaly table follows, then a report section that adds optional AI interpretation and exports Markdown with the run's provenance.

field.text: automated clustering and artifact screening of flow cytometry data in immunology

workflow.name: cluster a sample, flag the odd groups, and report them for review

steps.here: upload an FCS file or pick a bundled one; a spillover matrix stored in the file, or a matching CSV beside it, is found automatically

steps.step: set the computation's parameters and run it
steps.here: arcsinh cofactor slider, events-subsampled choice, metacluster count and random seed, then Run analysis: compensate, transform, FlowSOM-style clustering, UMAP

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: UMAP scatter coloured by cluster, cluster frequency bars, median-marker heatmap (clusters × markers) and a per-cluster table

steps.step: flag the items that stand out
steps.here: clusters flagged by frequency z-score and/or IsolationForest, listed with which test flagged them

steps.step: get a suggested reading of the flagged items
steps.here: optionally, an AI model calls each flagged cluster an artifact or a real population, citing marker evidence. A separate button proposes a hierarchical gating strategy from the marker panel
build the report with AI or detection-only and download it as Markdown, with the file's SHA-256 and every setting recorded

distinctive: Deterministic computation (compensation, transform, clustering) is kept separate from AI judgement, which is opt-in and applied only to clusters the statistics have already flagged.
The report works as a provenance receipt: the file checksum, cofactor, subsample size, seed and model used are recorded, so the run can be reproduced exactly.
A panel of pre-computed evaluation results, from a known-answer test with planted artifacts, shows how far each AI model can be trusted before the person uses it.
Artifact hypotheses particular to the field (dead cells, debris, doublets, spillover) are what the interpretation is asked to weigh against a real cell population.
